Subject: Operator seats for pilot — pricing ask

Hi Vanessa,

Initial thought: 40% is outside standard guardrails for operator-seat SKU. Ben/Marissa, what is the minimum discount we can approve in field? Aditya — can finance run the ARR math and show sensitivity on revenue protection if we offer this with multi-year conversion?

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-12-02T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Operator seats for pilot — pricing ask

Vanessa —

I recommend the following structured offer to balance growth and revenue protection:
- Pilot: 12 operator seats at 25% off list for 3 months.
- One-time PS credit: $18,000 (to cover onboarding) delivered as invoice credit, non-refundable.
- Convert: If they convert within 90 days post-pilot to a 36-month commitment, we grant an additional retroactive 10% discount (effectively 35% total) applied to remaining term.

Why this? Preserves list price floor while adding a clear incentive to convert. Anything beyond 35% needs VP/CFO waiver given our seat-level price guardrails.

Pro forma numbers (estimate):
- ARR if converted: $360k (using standard seat pricing)
- FY1 recognized revenue: ~$270k with phased conversion assumptions

If the execs want to go to 40%, they need an exception memo with comping rationale and a mitigation plan (minimum revenue guarantee or early termination fee).

— Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T07:50:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Operator seats for pilot — pricing ask

Thanks Ben — I agree with the structure. If we escalate to VP/CFO for a full 40% concession, finance will want:
- A binding minimum commitment (12 months effective minimum revenue if conversion occurs), or a one-time conversion fee to protect ARR
- PS credit capped and tied to milestone acceptance (completion of onboarding & go-live)
- Contract language requiring automatic conversion to the 36-month term with a non-cancellable period for at least 12 months after conversion or specified early termination penalties

I'll draft an internal memo for VP/CFO that frames the strategic benefit (vertical reference, integration into EHR) and proposed mitigations. I'll attach the proposed_rate_sheet.xlsx and suggested approval language.

Attachments: proposed_rate_sheet.xlsx

— Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Operations

Date: 2026-12-04T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Operator seats for pilot — pricing ask

Couple of asks before we route to execs:
1) Please confirm the precise ARR profile if they convert at the proposed structure (both 35% and 40% paths). Include monthly invoicing cadence assumptions.
2) Provide the redlined SOW from their legal (or our redline) so revenue can validate milestone-triggered PS credits.
3) Risk table: show downside if they churn after pilot vs. upside if they expand into additional product lines.

Also recommend the approval memo include a recommended signoff block with: VP Commercial or CRO, VP Finance, CFO (or VP Finance + CFO if CFO wants to sign), and a legal acceptance confirmation.

Can we aim to have the memo packaged for exec review by Monday EOD?

— Aditya

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Operator seat license variance clearance request — VP/CFO endorsement requested

VP Finance / CFO —

Request: Seeking VP/CFO endorsement for a limited pricing variance for PulseMed (Deal DL-PT-9812). The requested commercial variance is a pilot discount of 40% on operator-seat SKU plus a one-time PS credit. Below is a concise memo for your review.

Summary:
- Customer: PulseMed (healthcare integration partner)
- Scope: 12 operator seats for a 3-month pilot; conversion to a 36-month committed term upon success
- Standard list seat price: $1,000/mo per operator seat (example)
- Proposed commercial structure (field): 25% pilot discount + $18k PS credit + retroactive 10% on conversion (35% total)
- Customer ask: immediate 40% pilot discount + PS credit and conversion to 36 months

Recommendation: Approve a constrained variance under the following conditions (these are required to mitigate revenue risk):
1) Minimum revenue guarantee at conversion: customer must commit to at least 12 months non-cancellable after conversion or pay an early termination fee equal to 30% of remaining committed value.
2) PS credit cap: $18,000 tied to milestone acceptance (onboarding completion).
3) Conversion window: conversion must be executed within 90 days of pilot completion to qualify for additional retroactive discount.
4) Legal to include redlined SOW references and acceptance criteria; revenue to confirm ARR math.
5) Exec approval contingent on finance sign-off of modeled ARR sensitivity (attached).

If execs approve the full 40% (instead of the recommended up-to-35%), we request explicit CFO signoff confirming acceptance of upside/downside economics and that Sales will record a bespoke waiver in the deal file.

Attachments: proposed_rate_sheet.xlsx, PulseMed_SOW_draft.pdf, redlined_SOW_from_legal.pdf

Signoff options (please initial):
- VP Finance: ____________________
- CFO: ____________________

Thanks for reviewing — happy to sync live if helpful.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
